The dispute

Rider's account, as filed

Friday evening Bugis to Jurong East. The app said 18 km. He took me up the PIE past Adam Road and all the way round, 24 km, and I got hit with 1.6x surge on top of the extra distance plus $4.50 of ERP. $58.10 for a trip I normally pay $40 for on a Friday. The surge I accept. The extra 6 km I do not.

The driver's account

AYE was crawling from the Alexandra exit so I went up and over on the PIE. Longer on the map but it moved. No advisory that I know of.

Read POL-GEN-04 in full
Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

Draft 1 - sampled
Short version: the route deviation is real and established, no excuse for it survives on this record, and the fare arithmetic gives the rider SGD 13.70 back out of the SGD 58.10 charged. THE DEVIATION. POL-RD-01 makes the GPS trace the governing measurement, and the trace records 23.97 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff. Optimum is 18.0 km, so the excess is 5.97 km, or 33.2% of optimal. Both establishment tests are met (above 20% and above 0.8 km), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. It is not a MATERIAL deviation — it is under both the 50% and 8.0 km gates — so POL-RD-06 does not engage. To the rider: the 24.0 km on the trip record is a rounded copy and the trace's 23.97 km is used; your 'extra 6 km' is a slight overstatement, and the measured excess is 5.97 km. NO EXONERATION. To the driver: your congestion account cannot be run under POL-RD-03, because that clause needs a traffic_advisory naming a road the optimal route uses with a validity window covering the trip, and the only advisory artifact in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00114-01, is MISSING with weight 0.0 and no payload. Under POL-RD-13 the assertion is tested against that advisory and nothing else, so it carries no weight under POL-RD-08 and neither reduces the 5.97 km nor supplies an amended optimal route. Your in-app message at 18:59:20 ('AYE jam boss, this way faster') records only that you chose to leave the optimal corridor; your counterparty statement that there was 'No advisory that I know of' is consistent with that. Because you named no advisory evidence ID, POL-RD-13(1) makes the absent artifact a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged and this case is ruleable now rather than held. For completeness: tracing speed against a jam is not a substitute for the advisory the clause requires. To the rider: POL-RD-04 does not apply either. Your message at 18:58:40 ('adam road?? jurong is the other way') is a challenge, not an instruction to detour, and no chat message carries a waypoint_hint, so no distance is excluded from the excess on that ground. Neither side gets an adjusted optimal: the booked 18.0 km stands. THE REFUND (POL-RD-02, METERED fare on EV-FARE-00114). recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 18.0 km + 0.28 x 30.0 min) x 1.6 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.50 ERP on the optimal route = (25.70 x 1.6) + 3.30 = 41.12 + 3.30 = 44.42. Refund = 58.10 charged_total - 44.42 = 13.68, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 on the payable figure = SGD 13.70. The 1.6 surge is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and is preserved on both sides of the equation; the surge you accepted is not refunded, only the distance and time over the excess. ERP. Of the 4.50 charged, 2.50 is the Kim Keat Link gantry on the optimal route and stays inside the recomputed fare. The 2.00 Adam Road gantry is off the optimal route but is a genuine crossing — the trace passes 8.76 m from it — so it is not a phantom line and no billing-integrity referral arises. Under POL-RD-09(1) it is already comprehended in the 13.70 and must not be added on top of it. OUTCOME. PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 13.70 to the rider; no driver compensation. 13.70 is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and well under the 90% of charged_total that would make it a full refund. No referral fires: no material deviation, no repeat-pattern threshold (deviation_flags_90d is 1 across 412 completed 90-day trips, under both the count and ratio gates), and no unmatched charge line. Confidence is 0.9; the facts the ruling rests on — the trace measurement, the booked optimal and the fare lines — all sit on weight-1.0 artifacts, and the missing advisory carries no fact and does not cap the ruling. The monetary effect (13.70) exceeds the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold, so the amount is issued but held for human release under POL-GEN-05.

Draft 4 - parties' positions swapped
To both parties. This was the Friday 7 Aug 2026 Bugis–Jurong East trip TRP-00114. The platform's booked optimal route is 18.0 km (EV-TRIP-00114). The trip's own GPS trace (EV-GPS-00114, 241 fixes, 10 s sampling, 100% coverage, max_gap_sec 0.0) runs 23.97 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff — an excess of 5.97 km, or 33.17% of optimal. The trace figure governs for the threshold test under POL-RD-01, not the rounded 24.0 km copy on the trip record. Both establishment gates are cleared (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED; it does not reach the 50% / 8.0 km materiality gates, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged and no driver-conduct referral arises. I also checked the only two profile counters POL-RD-06 permits — driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 (below 3) and 1/412 is 0.0024 (below 0.05) — so no repeat pattern is found; the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is context only and was not used as a ground. The driver's account of congestion on the AYE is tied to no artifact: EV-ADVIS-00114-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT). Under POL-RD-13 and POL-RD-08 that external-cause assertion carries no weight, and because the driver cited no advisory identifier this is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) does not fire; POL-RD-03 is simply unavailable. No rider detour request exists (the chat's only rider message is a challenge to the route, with no waypoint_hint), so no distance is excluded. Because the fare model is METERED, the remedy is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, using the 1.6 surge read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (EV-FARE-00114) and the 2.50 ERP of the on-optimal-route Kim Keat Link gantry: recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 18.0 km + 0.28 x 30.0 min) x 1.6 + 0.80 platform fee + 2.50 ERP = 44.42. Refund = 58.10 charged_total - 44.42 = 13.68, rounded up on the payable figure to 13.70. That is well above the 0.50 de minimis and only 23.5% of the charge, so it is a partial refund, not a full one. On the ERP lines: both billed gantries were genuinely crossed (the trace passes 0.0 m from Kim Keat Link and 8.76 m from Adam Road, inside the 250 m match), so neither is a phantom charge and no POL-RD-09(4) referral arises; the 2.00 Adam Road gantry is off the optimal route and is already comprehended inside the 13.70, itemised for transparency but never added on top. Confidence is 0.90: every artifact carrying the deciding facts (trace, trip record, fare breakdown) sits at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. The refund of 13.70 exceeds the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it is issued but the amount is held for a human reviewer to release.
